mappings.note: Volume ratio of two separate cones from ratios of h and r. Comparison of a basic formula, not a combination or a recast.
Cone melted into a sphere - a change of solid form with volume conserved.
Immersed cube displaces its own volume and the water takes cylindrical shape; solved exactly like a recast. Not C-7.2-LO-3, because the cube and the water are not one composite body.
Cone surmounted on a hemisphere, volumes ADDED, with the cone's height deduced from the total height. Volume of a combination, so LO-3 and not LO-2 (no area is asked).
Flow through a pipe filling a pond: the cylindrical water column becomes a cuboidal layer. Volume conserved across a shape change, C-7.3-LO-3.
One conical heap: its volume, then its curved surface for the canvas. Two formulas on the SAME single solid, so still competency level; nothing is combined (LO-2/LO-3) and nothing recast.
Capacity of a glass = cylinder MINUS the raised hemispherical or conical bottom. Composite volume by subtraction, and the item compares the two composites, so LO-3.
Volume of the largest sphere inscribed in a solid hemisphere. Only the inscribed solid's volume is wanted, so no subtraction (not C-7.2-LO-3) and no melting.
Solid hemisphere: total surface area 3 pi r^2 gives r, then volume. One solid, area used only as a route to r.
Cuboid melted and recast into cubes; the count comes from equating volumes across the change of shape.
Conical tent: curved surface area converted to a length of 5 m wide cloth and a cost. One cone, no second solid to combine with.
Cylinder melted into many small balls - recast with a count.
Cylinder with a conical cavity of the same height and radius: remaining volume (2/3)pi r^2 h by subtraction. Composite volume, nothing melted.

Plates are FITTED, not melted, so C-7.3-LO-3 is wrong; the pairing with the next item is deliberate. Fit is poor - the real content is packing, which no outcome in this frame covers - and the stem needs the book's packing diagram, which is not carried with it.
The melted twin of the previous item: coins recast into one cylinder, so volume is conserved and the count follows. This contrast is why the two items must not share a code.
Clay cone reshaped into a sphere - one solid form to another.
Sphere melted and recast as a cylinder; height follows from equating volumes.
Solid sphere melted and recast as a cylinder of given radius - same conversion, different numbers.
One cone: curved surface area gives l, Pythagoras gives h, then volume. All three relations belong to a single basic solid.
One cylinder: total surface area 2 pi r(r + h) with r + h given recovers r, then volume. Single solid.
Cylindrical glass volume times six, answered in litres. One solid; the unit change alone does not make it the combination outcome C-7.2-LO-3.
Cylinder with h = r: volume gives h directly. Single solid.
Hollow cylinder on a hollow hemisphere, inner AND outer surfaces summed. Surface area of a combination of solids - LO-2, not LO-3, because no volume is wanted.
Cone surmounted on a hemisphere, volumes added with h = 2r. Volume of a combination; no surface area asked, so not LO-2.
Cylinder with a conical cavity: total surface area is base + cylinder curved + CONE curved, the flat top being gone. Surface of a composite, so LO-2 rather than LO-3.
